title: Mein Schulalltag (School Life)
description: Talk about your school day in German — classroom items, school subjects, the timetable, weekdays, telling the time, giving simple opinions, and a first look at der, die and das.

notes.heading: 📌 In the Classroom (Im Klassenzimmer)
notes.body:
Here are the things you need every school day:

| German | English |
|---|---|
| der Stift | the pen |
| der Bleistift | the pencil |
| der Kuli (der Kugelschreiber) | the biro / ballpoint pen |
| das Heft | the exercise book |
| das Buch | the book |
| die Tasche | the bag |
| der Rucksack | the rucksack |
| der Tisch | the table / desk |
| der Stuhl | the chair |
| die Tafel | the board |
| der Radiergummi | the rubber / eraser |
| die Schere | the scissors |
| der Lehrer / die Lehrerin | the (male / female) teacher |

Notice every noun has **der, die or das** in front of it — this is its gender, and you should always learn the word together with its article.

notes.heading: 🔑 der, die, das — Your First Genders
notes.body:
Every German noun is **masculine (der)**, **feminine (die)** or **neuter (das)**. Gender is mostly not logical — das Mädchen (the girl) is neuter! — so learn each noun with its article as one unit.

A few helpful patterns:
- People are often the gender you expect: der Vater, der Lehrer (masculine) — die Mutter, die Lehrerin (feminine)
- Words ending in **-ung, -heit, -keit, -schaft** are feminine: die Zeitung, die Freiheit
- Words ending in **-chen** are neuter: das Mädchen, das Büchlein
- Days, months and seasons are masculine: der Montag, der Mai, der Sommer

**All plurals take die**, whatever the singular gender: der Stift → die Stifte, das Heft → die Hefte, die Tasche → die Taschen.

German nouns are always written with a **capital letter**, even in the middle of a sentence.

notes.heading: 📌 School Subjects (Die Schulfächer)
notes.body:
| German | English |
|---|---|
| Mathe / die Mathematik | maths |
| Englisch | English |
| Deutsch | German |
| die Naturwissenschaften (Bio, Chemie, Physik) | the sciences |
| Sport | PE |
| Kunst | art |
| Musik | music |
| Informatik | computing / ICT |
| Geschichte | history |
| Erdkunde / Geografie | geography |
| Religion | RE |
| Französisch | French |

Useful phrases:
- **das Fach** = the subject; **mein Lieblingsfach** = my favourite subject
- *Ich habe heute Mathe.* — I have maths today. (Subjects are normally used **without** der/die/das.)
- *Mein Lieblingsfach ist Sport.* — My favourite subject is PE.

notes.heading: 🔑 The Timetable & Days of the Week (Der Stundenplan)
notes.body:
Your timetable is **der Stundenplan**; a lesson is **die Stunde**.

| German | English |
|---|---|
| der Montag | Monday |
| der Dienstag | Tuesday |
| der Mittwoch | Wednesday |
| der Donnerstag | Thursday |
| der Freitag | Friday |
| der Samstag (der Sonnabend) | Saturday |
| der Sonntag | Sunday |

To say **on** a day, use **am**: *Am Montag habe ich Englisch.* — On Monday I have English.

All days are masculine (der) and, like all nouns, start with a capital letter. The school week in German-speaking countries traditionally runs Monday to Friday: *Von Montag bis Freitag habe ich Schule.*

notes.heading: 🔑 Telling the Time (Uhrzeiten)
notes.body:
Ask: **Wie spät ist es?** or **Wie viel Uhr ist es?** — What time is it?

- Es ist zwei Uhr. — It is two o'clock.
- Es ist Viertel nach drei. — It is quarter past three (3:15).
- Es ist **halb vier**. — It is **half past three** (3:30)!
- Es ist Viertel vor fünf. — It is quarter to five (4:45).

⚠️ **The big trap:** German *halb vier* means half way **to** four, i.e. 3:30 — NOT 4:30. Think of the hourglass being half full on the way to four.

For the 24-hour clock (timetables, trains): *Der Zug kommt um vierzehn Uhr dreißig.* — The train arrives at 14:30.

Use **um** for at a time: *Die Schule beginnt um acht Uhr.* — School starts at eight o'clock.

notes.heading: 💡 Opinions: gern & nicht gern
notes.body:
The easiest way to say you like something is **gern** (literally gladly) after the verb:

- Ich lerne **gern** Mathe. — I like learning maths.
- Ich habe Sport **gern**. — I like PE.
- Ich habe Chemie **nicht gern**. — I do not like chemistry.

You can also use **mögen** (to like):
- Ich mag Musik. — I like music.
- Ich mag Hausaufgaben nicht. — I do not like homework.

Add a reason with **weil** (because) or **denn**:
- Ich habe Kunst gern, **weil** sie kreativ ist. (The verb *ist* goes to the end after weil!)
- Mathe ist mein Lieblingsfach, **denn** es ist logisch. (After denn the verb stays in second position.)

Remember: whatever comes first in the sentence, the conjugated verb is always the **second idea**.

notes.heading: ⚠️ Common Mistakes at School
notes.body:
Watch out for these classic Year 7 errors:

1. **Forgetting capital letters on nouns** — *ich habe ein Heft*, never *ich habe ein heft*. Every noun, everywhere, gets a capital.
2. **halb vier ≠ 4:30** — it is 3:30. German counts towards the next hour.
3. **Guessing genders** — der, die and das rarely follow logic; learn the article with the word. (*der* Stift, *das* Heft, *die* Tasche — three school items, three different genders!)
4. **Verb in the wrong place** — the conjugated verb is the second idea: *Heute habe ich Sport.* (NOT *Heute ich habe Sport.*)
5. **Using an article with subjects** — say *Ich habe Mathe*, not *Ich habe die Mathe*, when talking about your lessons.

✅ Check yourself: *Am Mittwoch um neun Uhr habe ich Informatik.* — On Wednesday at nine o'clock I have computing. Day (am), time (um), verb second — all correct!

flashcards.example: Der Stift ist blau. — The pen is blue.
Ich schreibe in mein Heft. — I write in my exercise book.
Meine Tasche ist schwer. — My bag is heavy.
Der Bleistift liegt auf dem Tisch. — The pencil is lying on the desk.
Der Radiergummi ist klein und rosa. — The rubber is small and pink.
Mein Lieblingsfach ist Kunst. — My favourite subject is art.
Der Stundenplan hängt an der Wand. — The timetable is hanging on the wall.
Am Montag habe ich Mathe. — On Monday I have maths.

flashcards.definition: the clock / the watch; o'clock when telling the time
flashcards.example: Es ist drei Uhr. — It is three o'clock.

flashcards.definition: half — halb acht means 7:30, half way TO eight
flashcards.example: Die Schule beginnt um halb neun. — School starts at half past eight.

flashcards.definition: gladly — put it after a verb to say you like doing it
flashcards.example: Ich lerne gern Deutsch. — I like learning German.
Die Lehrerin schreibt an die Tafel. — The teacher writes on the board.

questions.stem: What is der Stift in English?
questions.explanation: Der Stift is the pen. The pencil is der Bleistift and the rubber is der Radiergummi.

questions.stem: Which of these is a day of the week?
questions.explanation: Der Mittwoch is Wednesday. Die Stunde is a lesson/hour, das Heft is an exercise book, and September is a month, not a day.

questions.stem: Ich habe Sport gern — what is this person saying?
choices: I have a lot of sport.
questions.explanation: Gern after a verb means you like doing it, so Ich habe Sport gern = I like PE. Without gern it would just mean I have PE.

questions.stem: What is das Heft used for at school?
choices: It is the board the teacher writes on.
It is the exercise book you write in.
It is the bag you carry.
It is the rubber you erase with.
questions.explanation: Das Heft is the exercise book. The board is die Tafel, the bag is die Tasche and the rubber is der Radiergummi.

questions.stem: What gender is die Tasche (the bag)?
questions.explanation: Die is the feminine article, so die Tasche is a feminine noun. Der is masculine, das is neuter, and die is also used for all plurals.

questions.stem: Es ist halb fünf — what time is it?
questions.explanation: German halb fünf means half way TO five — 4:30. This is the classic trap: 5:30 in German is halb sechs.

questions.stem: Which is the correct article for Buch (book)?
questions.explanation: Das Buch is neuter. There is no logic to guess here — you simply learn the article together with the noun, which is why vocabulary lists always include der, die or das.

questions.stem: Am Dienstag habe ich Kunst — when does this person have art?
questions.explanation: Dienstag is Tuesday, and am + day means on that day. Donnerstag is Thursday and Mittwoch is Wednesday — easy to confuse because of the similar endings.

questions.stem: Die ___ sind neu. Which article fits all German plurals?
questions.explanation: Whatever the singular gender, every plural noun takes die: der Stift → die Stifte, das Heft → die Hefte, die Tasche → die Taschen.

questions.stem: Which sentence has the verb in the correct position?
questions.explanation: The conjugated verb must be the second idea in the sentence. If heute comes first, the verb (habe) comes second and the subject follows: Heute habe ich Englisch.

questions.stem: Es ist Viertel nach drei — what time is it?
questions.explanation: Viertel nach drei is quarter past three, 3:15. Nach means past/after. Quarter to three would be Viertel vor drei.

questions.stem: Wie spät ist es? Es ist Viertel vor sieben — what time is it?
questions.explanation: Viertel vor sieben is quarter TO seven — 6:45. Vor means before/to, nach means past, and halb sieben would be 6:30.

questions.stem: Which sentence about opinions is correct German?
choices: Ich habe nicht gern Chemie, aber ich habe Bio gern.
questions.explanation: Nicht gern goes together after the verb: Ich habe Chemie nicht gern / Ich habe nicht gern Chemie. The other options scramble gern into positions German never uses.

questions.stem: Which is the natural way to talk about your favourite subject?
questions.explanation: School subjects are normally used without an article: Mein Lieblingsfach ist Informatik. Das Fach is neuter, so it takes mein, not meine.

questions.stem: Which sentence puts the day, time and verb in correct German order?
choices: Die Schule am Montag beginnt um acht Uhr.
Am Montag die Schule beginnt um acht Uhr.
Am Montag um acht Uhr beginnt die Schule.
Beginnt die Schule am Montag um acht Uhr.
questions.explanation: With time expressions first, the verb stays second and the subject follows it: Am Montag um acht Uhr beginnt die Schule. The other options push the verb out of position two.
